title: 11. Numeracy & Number Systems: Multi-Digit Addition with Regrouping
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Add two two-digit whole numbers with regrouping in the ones place.
questions.question: What is \(47+38\)?
questions.explanation: Add the ones digits: \(7+8=15\). Write \(5\) in the ones place and regroup \(1\) ten. Add the tens digits, including the regrouped ten: \(4+3+1=8\). Therefore, \(47+38=85\).
questions.hint: Add the ones digits first, and regroup if the sum is \(10\) or more.

questions.learningObjective: Add two two-digit whole numbers with regrouping in the ones place.
questions.question: What is \(56+27\)?
questions.explanation: Add the ones digits: \(6+7=13\). Write \(3\) in the ones place and regroup \(1\) ten. Add the tens digits, including the regrouped ten: \(5+2+1=8\). Therefore, \(56+27=83\).
questions.hint: Regroup \(10\) ones as \(1\) ten when the ones sum is \(10\) or more.

questions.learningObjective: Add two three-digit whole numbers with regrouping in the ones and tens places.
questions.question: What is \(246+178\)?
questions.explanation: Add the ones digits: \(6+8=14\). Write \(4\) in the ones place and regroup \(1\) ten. Add the tens digits, including the regrouped ten: \(4+7+1=12\). Write \(2\) in the tens place and regroup \(1\) hundred. Add the hundreds digits, including the regrouped hundred: \(2+1+1=4\). Therefore, \(246+178=424\).
questions.hint: Work from right to left and regroup whenever a column sum reaches \(10\) or more.

questions.learningObjective: Add two three-digit whole numbers with regrouping in the ones and tens places.
questions.question: What is \(375+268\)?
questions.explanation: Add the ones digits: \(5+8=13\). Write \(3\) and regroup \(1\) ten. Add the tens digits, including the regrouped ten: \(7+6+1=14\). Write \(4\) and regroup \(1\) hundred. Add the hundreds digits, including the regrouped hundred: \(3+2+1=6\). Therefore, \(375+268=643\).
questions.hint: Regroup from the ones place to the tens place, and from the tens place to the hundreds place when needed.

questions.learningObjective: Add two four-digit whole numbers with regrouping in multiple places.
questions.question: What is \(2{,}458+1{,}376\)?
questions.explanation: Add the ones digits: \(8+6=14\). Write \(4\) and regroup \(1\) ten. Add the tens digits, including the regrouped ten: \(5+7+1=13\). Write \(3\) and regroup \(1\) hundred. Add the hundreds digits, including the regrouped hundred: \(4+3+1=8\). Add the thousands digits: \(2+1=3\). Therefore, \(2{,}458+1{,}376=3{,}834\).
questions.hint: Add column by column from right to left, carrying when a column sum is \(10\) or more.

questions.learningObjective: Add two four-digit whole numbers with regrouping involving zero digits.
questions.question: What is \(5{,}306+2{,}897\)?
questions.explanation: Add the ones digits: \(6+7=13\). Write \(3\) and regroup \(1\) ten. Add the tens digits, including the regrouped ten: \(0+9+1=10\). Write \(0\) and regroup \(1\) hundred. Add the hundreds digits, including the regrouped hundred: \(3+8+1=12\). Write \(2\) and regroup \(1\) thousand. Add the thousands digits, including the regrouped thousand: \(5+2+1=8\). Therefore, \(5{,}306+2{,}897=8{,}203\).
questions.hint: Do not skip a zero digit; include it when adding each column.

questions.learningObjective: Add three four-digit whole numbers with regrouping.
questions.question: What is \(1{,}248+3{,}675+2{,}089\)?
questions.explanation: Add the ones digits: \(8+5+9=22\). Write \(2\) and regroup \(2\) tens. Add the tens digits, including the regrouped tens: \(4+7+8+2=21\). Write \(1\) and regroup \(2\) hundreds. Add the hundreds digits, including the regrouped hundreds: \(2+6+0+2=10\). Write \(0\) and regroup \(1\) thousand. Add the thousands digits, including the regrouped thousand: \(1+3+2+1=7\). Therefore, \(1{,}248+3{,}675+2{,}089=7{,}012\).
questions.hint: Add all numbers column by column, carrying the full amount when a column sum is \(10\) or more.

questions.learningObjective: Solve a word problem by adding two four-digit whole numbers with regrouping.
questions.question: A library has \(3{,}478\) books. It receives \(1{,}569\) more books. How many books does the library have now?
questions.explanation: Add the two amounts: \(3{,}478+1{,}569\). Add the ones digits: \(8+9=17\). Write \(7\) and regroup \(1\) ten. Add the tens digits, including the regrouped ten: \(7+6+1=14\). Write \(4\) and regroup \(1\) hundred. Add the hundreds digits, including the regrouped hundred: \(4+5+1=10\). Write \(0\) and regroup \(1\) thousand. Add the thousands digits, including the regrouped thousand: \(3+1+1=5\). Therefore, \(3{,}478+1{,}569=5{,}047\) books.
questions.hint: Identify the two addends in the problem, then add them using regrouping.

questions.learningObjective: Add two four-digit whole numbers with regrouping that produces a five-digit sum.
questions.question: What is \(6{,}785+4{,}376\)?
questions.explanation: Add the ones digits: \(5+6=11\). Write \(1\) and regroup \(1\) ten. Add the tens digits, including the regrouped ten: \(8+7+1=16\). Write \(6\) and regroup \(1\) hundred. Add the hundreds digits, including the regrouped hundred: \(7+3+1=11\). Write \(1\) and regroup \(1\) thousand. Add the thousands digits, including the regrouped thousand: \(6+4+1=11\). Write \(1\) in the thousands place and carry \(1\) to the ten-thousands place. Therefore, \(6{,}785+4{,}376=11{,}161\).
questions.hint: When the thousands column sum is \(10\) or more, the answer will have a ten-thousands digit.

questions.learningObjective: Add three four-digit whole numbers with regrouping in multiple columns.
questions.question: What is \(2{,}487+3{,}596+1{,}845\)?
questions.explanation: Add the ones digits: \(7+6+5=18\). Write \(8\) and regroup \(1\) ten. Add the tens digits, including the regrouped ten: \(8+9+4+1=22\). Write \(2\) and regroup \(2\) hundreds. Add the hundreds digits, including the regrouped hundreds: \(4+5+8+2=19\). Write \(9\) and regroup \(1\) thousand. Add the thousands digits, including the regrouped thousand: \(2+3+1+1=7\). Therefore, \(2{,}487+3{,}596+1{,}845=7{,}928\).
questions.hint: Add column by column from right to left, and carry the full regrouped amount to the next column.
